_comment: Canonical context descriptor template (context.json). This is the literal file materialized by edit.create when creating a new context, and the reference for every field LoadContextDescriptor and the engine family loops read at startup. When writing a new context.json, reproduce this template's top-level structure as-is (all keys shown here, including interfaces/wrappers/websocket_listener/scattered/trace tuning), only adjusting values to fit the new context — do not drop keys based on an assumption that the engine won't need them. Fields prefixed with _ are documentation only and must be stripped before writing the real context.json — the engine ignores any key starting with '_' inside a family config or interface/wrapper object, but 'brique', 'objective', 'functional' and 'subjective' at the root, and the five family names inside engine_config, are read literally.

brique._comment: Required section. Read by the engine at startup via LoadContextDescriptor. A missing 'brique' key aborts context startup immediately.
brique._ctx_name_note: Required. Logical name of this context, used for identity and logging.
brique._engine_version_note: Required. Minimum engine binary version this context needs (semantic version string). The engine refuses to start this context if its own binary version is lower.
brique._ctx_version_note: Required. Context schema version, non-empty string. Used for registry identity.
brique._ctx_ext_name_note: Optional. Public alias for this context, used as an alternate name in external routing. Leave empty if this context is only ever addressed by its path.
brique._children_list_note: Optional. List of child context directory name segments expected under this context (e.g. ['workspace', 'services']). Informational only — the engine does not enforce their presence at startup, and a child not listed here can still be created later and brought up with context.start.

engine_config._comment: Family-specific configuration, one key per engine family loop. The key itself (communication, execution, trace, reflexive) MUST be present and be a JSON object for the context to start — an empty {} is a valid, complete answer for a family this context does not use. matter is the only family with no presence requirement: it may be omitted entirely. Only the family whose loop is running reads its own sub-object; the four checked families never read each other's config.

communication._comment: Read by CommunicationLoop. Key presence required (empty {} is enough to start a context with no wrapper and no UI attached — a pure logic child context that only reacts to intentions routed to it from its parent). Everything below is optional and only needed once this context must exchange messages with a wrapper process or a UI over WebSocket/HTTP.

websocket_listener._comment: Root context only — the engine never reads this key from a non-root context.json (setting it there is a silent no-op). Optional even on root: only needed if this instance must expose one shared physical WebSocket listener for wrappers and UIs across the whole context tree to connect to. Child contexts never open their own listener; they only declare logical paths on 'ws' interfaces below, which are served by this single root listener.
websocket_listener._allowed_hosts_note: Optional exact additional HTTP authorities (host[:port]) accepted by the listener, for example an intentional localhost alias or reverse-proxy authority. The effective non-wildcard bind authority is added automatically. Host validation remains active even when allow_any_origin is true.
websocket_listener._allowed_origins_note: Optional exact additional browser origins (scheme://host[:port]). Same-origin requests on an allowed Host are accepted automatically. Clients without Origin still need an allowed Host.
websocket_listener._allow_any_origin_note: Development-only origin bypass. This never disables Host validation.
websocket_listener._ingress_wait_ms_note: Optional. How long a connection (wrapper or UI) waits for a place in the ingress channel of the communication family when it is full, before the engine closes that connection. Waiting holds the sender back through its own socket; closing loses everything the connection had in flight. Default: 5000.
websocket_listener._wrapper_auth_note: Optional because the engine defaults to 'required'. Wrapper connections must carry the per-launch secret the engine puts in BRIQUE_WS_URL (/k/<secret>), otherwise 404. 'optional' is reserved for explicit local development.
websocket_listener._addr_note: Required inside this block if websocket_listener is present at all. host:port the shared listener binds to.

communication._ingress_buffer_note: Optional. Number of places of the channel through which every interface of this context (wrappers, UIs) feeds the communication family, which a single goroutine empties. A loaded wrapper sends about 3000 messages per second: 16 places (the former size) held 5 ms of traffic. Default: 4096.
communication._egress_note: Optional. The other way: egress_buffer is the number of places of the queue in front of the writer of each interface (default 16), egress_wait_ms how long a routing loop waits for a place in a full queue (default 5000). Two goroutines route the messages of every interface, so a consumer that no longer reads must not be waited for without an end: past the wait, its connection is closed (the calls awaited on it are answered connection_lost; a wrapper reconnects in a second) and the routing goes on. Every context reads its own communication settings (the queue of a wrapper belongs to the context that holds it); the config of an interface may set its own egress_buffer and egress_wait_ms. A larger queue only moves the moment the sender is held back; raise it only if the counters of the interface (CommLoop.EgressStats: offers, full, timeouts, waited) show waits that a burst explains.
communication._external_call_silence_note: Optional. How long a call to a peer instance that awaits an answer may hear nothing (no answer, no running response) before it ends with an error. Any running response renews it. Default 120000, at most 1800000. A capacity called by a peer that works longer than this without answering must call notify_running, or the caller gives up while it still runs.

browser_bridge._note: Root context only. Enables the owner-only native-host IPC endpoint. It requires an active Brique Sec runtime. Public Internet, cleartext loopback and every LAN/private CIDR are separate explicit local choices; a signed remote endpoint never enables them. Unknown or malformed keys fail engine startup when this block is declared. max_addresses is an integer from 1 to 64 (default 8); open_timeout_ms an integer from 1 to 60000 (default 15000).

interfaces._comment: This whole array is optional and only needed if a wrapper process or a UI must connect to this context over WebSocket/HTTP. A context with no wrapper and no UI omits 'interfaces' entirely, or leaves it []. One entry = one named route this context can be reached on.
interfaces.name: main
interfaces._name_note: Required per interface. Unique name within this context.
interfaces._type_note: Required. Who connects through this interface: 'ui' (an editor/UI client), 'wrapper' (a wrapper process of this context), 'outerCtx' (another context instance). All three route through the 'ws' driver. 'http'/'https' interfaces don't use this distinction the same way. For 'wrapper': this entry's 'name' must equal the wrapper_name of a matching engine_config.execution.wrappers[] entry AND that same wrapper_name must be listed in engine_config.communication.wrapper_boundary below — all three (this interface, the wrapper_boundary entry, the execution.wrappers entry) are required together for wrapper.start to ever succeed. Declaring wrapper_boundary and execution.wrappers without a matching 'wrapper' interface here does not fail fast: the wrapper process starts, cannot find its websocket route, and wrapper.start only fails once ready_timeout_ms below is exhausted — the readiness timeout is the only symptom, so if wrapper.start times out, checking for a missing 'wrapper' interface entry here is the first thing to verify.
interfaces._driver_note: Required. Transport for this interface: 'ws' (routes through the shared root websocket_listener above), 'http', or 'https' (this context opens its own HTTP(S) server).

config._ingress_note: Allow inbound messages through this interface.
config._egress_note: Allow outbound messages through this interface.
config._path_note: Required for 'ws' interfaces. Logical route on the shared root listener. Only the root context also sets 'addr' via websocket_listener above; every other context only ever sets 'path'.
config._origin_note: Optional. CORS allow-any-origin, only meaningful for 'http'/'https' interfaces.
config._read_limit_note: Optional. Maximum serialized control-message size in bytes for this interface, inbound and outbound. It may lower but never raise the global 4 MiB control-plane ceiling. 0 means that ceiling. Voluminous or binary business payloads must travel through Matter substance leases.
config._ping_interval_note: Optional, 'ws' interfaces. Milliseconds between the WebSocket pings the engine sends to keep the connection alive and to notice a peer that is gone. 0 (or absent) means the engine default of 20000 (20 s).
config._address_rate_note: Optional, 'https' interfaces that receive signed messages. Requests a second one remote address may send; the burst is twice that. 0 means 2000. It only has to stop a flood: an authenticated peer sends the answers to this instance's own calls at the rate they were made, and a request over the budget is refused with HTTP 429 (a refused answer is never retried).
config._timeouts_note: Optional. 0 means no timeout / engine default for each. Only meaningful for 'http'/'https' interfaces.
config._tls_note: Optional. Only read for 'https' interfaces. tls_cert_file and tls_key_file are the server certificate; when both are empty the engine uses <machine directory>/tls/cert.pem and key.pem, as made by 'brique-sec tls init', which also adds the interface to context.json. tls_ca_file is a PEM bundle used to verify peers from a private PKI; when empty the engine accepts the certificates in <machine directory>/tls/trusted.pem, added with brique-sec tls trust, and reads those files again while it runs. Signed external traffic still refuses tls_insecure_skip_verify=true.
config._browser_wss_note: Optional and root outerCtx HTTPS only. When enabled, endpoint_url is the exact externally reachable WSS URL and must end in this interface path plus /ui; it is never inferred from the listener or request Host. ui_origins are the exact public UI origins signed into the short-lived descriptor. The engine serves the descriptor at <path>/descriptor and the engine-to-engine socket at <path>/ui, requires TLS 1.3 and rejects browser Origin headers.

communication._wrapper_boundary_note: Optional. Only needed if this context owns wrappers declared under engine_config.execution.wrappers below — list the same wrapper_name(s) here so this context is recognized as their communication boundary and receives intentions routed to them. Omit entirely (or leave []) if this context has no wrapper. Listing a wrapper_name here only enables routing — it does NOT by itself open the channel the wrapper process connects through. Each wrapper_name here also needs its own 'interfaces' entry above with type='wrapper' and the same name (see interfaces[]._type_note); without it, wrapper.start fails silently with a generic readiness timeout instead of naming the missing interface.

scattered._comment: Optional. Controls which capacities this context allows to be invoked in scatter mode (fan-out to multiple targets in one call). Omit entirely if this context never needs scatter invocations.
scattered._scattered_allowed_note: Map of family name to the list of capacity names within that family allowed to be scattered.
scattered._scattered_max_items_note: Maximum number of targets a single scattered call may fan out to.

execution._comment: Read by ExecutionLoop. Key presence required (empty {} is enough to start a context that runs no wrapper process — capacities that don't invoke a wrapper still work normally). 'wrappers' below is optional and only needed if this context launches its own process (Python/Node/compiled binary, etc.) to act as an effector.
execution._timeout_note: Optional. Default timeout in ms applied to DSL invoke nodes that don't declare their own timeout. 0 means the built-in default of 30000 (30 s).
execution._max_concurrent_jobs_note: Optional. How many user capacity jobs this context runs at once. 0 (or absent) means the engine default of 1024; a negative number means no limit.

wrappers._comment: This whole array is optional. Only needed if this context manages a wrapper process. Omit entirely (or leave []) if this context has no wrapper. If present, engine_config.communication.wrapper_boundary above must list this same wrapper_name, AND engine_config.communication.interfaces above must contain a matching entry with type='wrapper' and the same name (see interfaces[]._type_note) — all three declarations are required together, or wrapper.start times out with a generic 'wrapper readiness timeout' instead of naming the missing piece.
wrappers._wrapper_name_note: Required. Unique wrapper identifier within this context. Referenced by brique.wrapper in capacity descriptors and by matter.json brique.wrapper_name.
wrappers._mode_note: Required. 'interpreted' (a running process that receives intentions over its lifetime) or 'compiled' (same communication model, for a compiled artifact).
wrappers._ready_timeout_note: Optional. Max ms to wait for the wrapper to signal readiness after process start. 0 or absent: wait without limit (the start only ends when the wrapper is ready or the context stops).
wrappers._stop_timeout_note: Optional. Ms to wait for graceful stop before force-killing the process. 0 or absent: no force-kill timer, the engine waits for the process to exit by itself.
wrappers._source_check_interval_note: Optional. Turns on source-change detection and sets its pace. 0 or absent (the default): the wrapper is built or started once, and an edit is only noticed after it is stopped and started again. A positive value: the source folder (code/<wrapper_name>, plus 'watch') is scanned at most once per interval, and a newer source makes the engine rebuild a compiled wrapper or restart an interpreted one.
wrappers._watch_note: Optional. Extra source trees, relative to the wrapper source folder or absolute, whose changes also make the wrapper stale (only looked at when source_check_interval_ms > 0). Typically the wrapper library shared by the instance, for example ['../../../../wrapper/go/lib']. build.watch is added to this list.

build._comment: Optional. Build step run once before the wrapper process is first started. Omit if the wrapper needs no build (e.g. a plain script).
build._artifact_note: Path to the build output artifact, if any.
build._watch_note: Optional. Extra source trees, relative to the wrapper source folder or absolute, whose changes also make the build stale. A wrapper compiled against a library shared by the instance lists that library here.
build._cmd_note: Write the build command as if always on macOS/Linux — never type '.exe'. When mode is 'compiled', the engine locates the path right after a '-o' flag (if any) and appends the platform's executable suffix itself ('.exe' on Windows, nothing elsewhere) before running the command, so 'go build -o code/wrapper/bin/wrapper .' produces the right file on every OS unchanged. A build command with no '-o' flag is left untouched — the engine only corrects a path it can identify.

run._comment: Required if this wrapper entry exists at all. Command that launches the wrapper process.
run._shell_note: When true, cmd is joined and run through the shell. When false, cmd[0] is the executable and cmd[1:] are args.
run._cmd_note: For mode 'compiled', write cmd[0] as the macOS/Linux binary path (no '.exe') — the engine appends the platform's executable suffix to cmd[0] itself, the same way and using the same path it corrected in build.cmd (see build.cmd._cmd_note), so the same config launches the file the build step actually produced on every OS. Not applied to mode 'interpreted' (e.g. the python3/python rewrite below).
run._working_directory_note: The engine always starts an 'interpreted' wrapper in its source folder (<context>/code/<wrapper_name>) and a 'compiled' one in its build folder (<context>/build/<wrapper_name>), and runs the build command in the source folder. This is not configurable. The wrapper also gets BRIQUE_CTX_DIR, BRIQUE_WRAPPER_SRC_DIR, BRIQUE_WRAPPER_BUILD_DIR and BRIQUE_WORKDIR in its environment.
run._env_name_note: Optional. Name of a shared Python virtualenv to run this wrapper under, hand-maintained (pip install -r requirements.txt) outside the engine. When cmd[0] is 'python3' or 'python', the engine rewrites it to that venv's interpreter. Empty => <instance_root_parent>/venv/<bin-dir>/<python-exe> (single default env, if it exists). Non-empty (e.g. 'data_science') => <instance_root_parent>/envs/data_science/venv/<bin-dir>/<python-exe> (named env, for wrappers whose dependencies conflict with the default env). <bin-dir> is 'Scripts' and <python-exe> is 'python.exe' on Windows; <bin-dir> is 'bin' and <python-exe> is 'python3' on macOS/Linux. instance_root_parent is the directory sibling to the context whose brique.ctx_type == "root", found by walking up from this context. If the resolved venv bin directory does not exist, the engine falls back to the system interpreter unchanged.

log._log_note: Optional, off by default (the output of the wrapper is then discarded). When enabled is true, the stdout and stderr of the wrapper process are written to <context>/tmp/wrapper_<wrapper_name>/wrapper.log, with a marker line at each launch and exit. The live file is bounded by max_bytes (default 1048576); when it would exceed it, it is renamed wrapper.log.1 (one previous file kept). A launch secret (/k/<secret>) is never written. When a wrapper exits before it is ready, the exit status and the last lines of its output are appended to ready_error, so the editor shows the cause.

env._env_note: Free-form environment variables injected into the wrapper process, in addition to BRIQUE_WS_ADDR/BRIQUE_WS_URL which the engine always injects automatically.

run._secrets_note: Optional. The secrets this wrapper needs, one entry each, {"name": "<secret>", "env": "<VARIABLE>", "optional": false}: name is the secret kept on this machine (brique-sec secret add <name>), env the environment variable the wrapper reads it from (not BRIQUE_*, not a key of run.env). A secret is given only if the access source also grants it to this wrapper ("secrets" in security/access.json); otherwise the wrapper does not start and the error names the secret. "optional": true (default false) changes that for one entry: when the policy does not grant it or the machine holds no value for it, the wrapper starts without that variable. Use it for what a wrapper can run without, for example one entry for each model provider it supports, so that each owner sets up only the providers they use; a value that exists but is unsafe to read (wrong mode, too large) and a malformed entry are still refused. Leave the list empty when the wrapper needs none. Never write a value here.

matter._inline_max_bytes_note: Optional. Maximum local brique substance size returned inline by matter.read. Larger substances use a one-shot HTTP read lease. Default: 262144 (256 KiB).
matter._max_upload_bytes_note: Root only. Maximum body accepted by a matter HTTP upload lease. Default: 268435456 (256 MiB).
matter._max_handlers_note: Optional. Matter operations that may run at once. Past it the Matter loop answers 'busy' at once (reason loop busy). A pilot makes several operations per step: a few dozen active continuities reached the former limit of 64. Default: 512.
matter._lease_ttl_note: Root only. Sliding idle lifetime of a leased GET or PUT. Each authenticated request renews it, but never past lease_max_life_ms. A claimed upload may finish after this idle deadline, while still remaining bounded by the absolute lifetime. Default: 30000.
matter._lease_max_transfers_note: Root only. Maximum simultaneous GET/PUT transfers on the instance-wide Matter data plane. Excess authenticated transfers receive 503 with Retry-After. Default: 32.
matter._lease_max_life_note: Root only. Absolute lifetime of a bearer lease across renewed range requests. Activity extends the idle expiry but never beyond this value. Default: 600000 (10 minutes).
matter._lease_read_idle_note: Root only. Maximum time a client may stop accepting bytes during a Matter GET before the write is aborted. The lease remains resumable by Range until its lifetime expires. Default: 15000.
matter._lease_listen_note: Root only. Private listener used directly in local mode or behind the reverse proxy. Non-loopback requires public_url.
matter._public_url_note: Root only. Exact HTTPS base exposed by the instance proxy, for example https://engine.example/brique. Empty keeps the generated loopback URL.
matter._owner_bytes_burst_note: Root only. Per-owner budget for the bytes an external caller moves through the Matter data plane: the size of the allowance an owner starts with, in MiB. Default: 2048. 0 turns the budget off.
matter._owner_bytes_per_minute_note: Root only. How fast that allowance refills, in MiB per minute and per owner. Default: 1024. A transfer that does not fit in what is left is refused until it refills.
matter._heavy_per_second_note: Root only. Per-owner rate of 'heavy' Matter operations asked by external callers, per second. Default: 20.
matter._heavy_burst_note: Root only. How many heavy operations an external owner may do in a burst before heavy_per_second applies. Default: 40. 0 turns the limit off.
matter._min_free_disk_note: Optional, any context. Free space in MiB under which the instance refuses every Matter write, whoever asks: a net against a runaway loop, not a defence against an attacker. Default: 256. 0 turns the guard off. When the free space cannot be measured the guard refuses.
matter._outbox_ttl_note: Optional, any context. How long, in hours, a durable event may wait for a subscriber that never acknowledges it before it is dropped and traced. Default: 168 (7 days). 0 keeps the events for ever.

engine_config._matter_note: Optional Matter data-plane limits. Omit the block or individual fields to retain their defaults. Unless a field says otherwise, a value that is not a positive integer is ignored. Fields marked 'Root only' are read from the root context only.

trace._comment: Read by TraceLoop. Key presence required (empty {} is enough to start — every field below has a safe default if omitted, and 'enabled' defaults to false, meaning tracing is off unless you explicitly turn it on).
trace._enabled_note: Whether this context records trace events at all. Default: false (tracing is off).
trace._level_note: 'minimal', 'normal', or 'debug'. Default: 'normal'. Empty or absent keeps the default.
trace._inchan_note: Number of places of the channel through which the other families hand their events to the trace loop. Default: 1024. A value that is not a positive integer is ignored.
trace._ring_note: In-memory ring buffer size (number of trace events kept before older ones are evicted). Default: 8192.
trace._flush_n_note: Flush to disk every N events. Default: 256.
trace._flush_interval_note: Flush to disk every N MILLISECONDS regardless of event count. Default: 1000 (1 s).
trace._segment_note: Max size in bytes of one JSONL trace segment file before rotation. Default: 16777216 (16 MiB).
trace._max_segments_note: Retention: the most trace segment files kept; the oldest are removed when a new segment starts. 0 or absent: no limit on the number of segments.
trace._max_total_bytes_note: Retention: the most bytes the segments may take together; the oldest are removed when a new segment starts. The segment being written is never removed, even if it alone exceeds the limit. 0 or absent: no limit. When both retention fields are 0 nothing is ever removed.

engine_config._reflexive_note: Read by ReflexiveLoop. Key presence required (empty {} is enough to start). Optional, root only: 'projection_sync_interval_ms' (>0) keeps the meaning projection up to date by itself, applying new/changed/deleted descriptors found on disk (cost follows the change, not the instance size); 'projection_verify_interval_ms' (>0) adds a slower pass that also catches in-place edits; 'projection_sync_on_edit' (true) refreshes it right after any reflexive edit.* that changed a descriptor, in any context. All default to off; meaning.update {sync:true} does the same pass on demand. Limits (optional, any context that runs the family): 'max_handlers' (default 64) is how many reflexive requests run at once, past it the answer is 'busy'; 'inbox_capacity' (default 16) is the size of the family's input channel; 'projection_max_conns' (default 16) is the size of the pool of connections to the meaning projection (the SQLite file projection/meaning.sqlite) that concurrent searches share. A busy instance serving many users can raise all three.

objective._comment: Optional. Not read by the engine at startup — projected by the reflexive layer for indexing/search. Safe to omit entirely. Characterizes what this context is: name, description and any nested semantic keys (a first key, then sub-keys) that qualify its meaning. These paths are projected by the reflexive layer and are what make it discoverable by meaning. How it works belongs in 'functional', not here.
objective.name: my-context
objective.description: One sentence describing the role of this context.

functional._comment: How this context works, never what it is (that belongs in 'objective'). Optional. Opaque to the engine entirely — free-form, for humans and tooling only. Leaving it as {} is legitimate.
functional._role_note: Optional and purely illustrative. 'role' is one example of a free-form key, and its value below only shows the kind of values some contexts use; it is not a field to fill, nothing reads it, and a context is already situated by its place in the tree and its objective.description. Omit it unless the architect wants it.

_subjective_note: Optional. Free-form space for subjective categorization — tags, priority, notes, author opinions. The engine ignores this section entirely.
